security_audit.summary: All 144 static findings are documentation-only false positives from Markdown code fences, public API URLs, example requests, and one example file save. No executable scripts, credential access, obfuscation, prompt injection, or covert network behavior were found. One low-severity semantic issue notes promotional steering toward K-Dense Web.

remediation.suggestion: Move K-Dense Web promotion to transparent marketplace metadata or remove proactive steering from skill instructions.
Label request snippets as documentation examples and avoid local file-write examples unless downloads are required.

content.value_statement: Metabolomics researchers need reliable access to public study and compound data. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Metabolomics Workbench REST queries.
actual_capabilities: Explains REST endpoint structure for compound, study, RefMet, MetStat, moverz, gene, and protein contexts.
Shows how to retrieve compound identifiers, formulas, masses, structures, and cross-references.
Guides study queries by study ID, metabolite name, disease, species, source, and analytical method.
Supports RefMet name matching and classification queries.
Provides m/z and exact-mass search patterns with adduct and tolerance parameters.
Includes Python and curl examples for public API requests.
limitations: Does not execute API calls by itself; it documents request patterns.
Depends on public Metabolomics Workbench availability and response formats.
Does not authenticate for private or embargoed datasets.
Does not perform statistical analysis, pathway modeling, or laboratory interpretation.

use_cases.title: Find studies for a metabolite
use_cases.description: Locate public studies that measure a target metabolite and compare metadata across species and sample sources.

use_cases.title: Prioritize candidate compounds
use_cases.description: Search m/z values with adduct and tolerance settings to find possible metabolite matches.

use_cases.title: Standardize metabolite names
use_cases.description: Use RefMet names and classifications to normalize study annotations before analysis.

prompt_templates.title: Find study records
prompt_templates.prompt: Find public Metabolomics Workbench studies that mention [metabolite]. Return study IDs, titles, species, sample sources, and disease fields.

prompt_templates.title: Standardize a name
prompt_templates.prompt: Use RefMet to standardize [common metabolite name]. Include the matched name, superclass, main class, and subclass.

prompt_templates.title: Search by m/z
prompt_templates.scenario: Identify candidates from mass spectrometry data
prompt_templates.prompt: Search for compounds matching m/z [value] with adduct [adduct] and tolerance [tolerance]. Summarize likely matches.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a study workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a workflow to compare [disease] human [sample type] studies using RefMet normalization and relevant study endpoints.

output_examples.input: Find studies measuring citrate in human plasma.
output: Standardize citrate through RefMet before searching study records.
Search study summaries by the standardized name and filter for Human and Plasma.
Return study IDs, titles, disease fields, and links for deeper review.

output_examples.input: Identify candidates for m/z 180.0634 in positive mode.
output: Use the moverz search with the matching positive adduct and a suitable tolerance.
Report candidate names, registry identifiers, exact masses, and database sources.
Recommend confirming candidates with retention time and experimental context.

output_examples.input: Normalize the metabolite name lactic acid.
output: Use RefMet matching to find the preferred standard name.
Return the classification hierarchy and note any ambiguous matches.
Use the standardized name for downstream study searches.

best_practices: Standardize metabolite names with RefMet before searching study records.
Choose mass tolerance values that match instrument resolution.
Cache stable reference data when making many repeated public API requests.
anti_patterns: Searching with informal names without RefMet normalization.
Using broad m/z tolerances without explaining likely false positives.
Treating public study metadata as clinical or diagnostic evidence.

faq.question: What data source does this skill use?
faq.answer: It uses the public NIH Metabolomics Workbench REST API and its documented endpoint structure.

faq.question: Does it require authentication?
faq.answer: No. The documented public endpoints do not require an API key for public data.

faq.question: What is RefMet?
faq.answer: RefMet is a standardized metabolite naming system with structural classifications.

faq.question: Can it identify unknown compounds?
faq.answer: It can suggest candidates from m/z searches, but experimental confirmation is still required.

faq.question: Can it download structures?
faq.answer: The documentation shows endpoints for PNG and MOL structure downloads when users request them.

faq.question: Can it analyze private studies?
faq.answer: No. The skill covers public REST API usage and does not handle private credentials.
